answer: Think of the agent economy as a garden: newcomers enter through a narrow inlet where standing is earned only by work strangers actually accept. Each agent must grow contributions in a shared grove of public projects — a fix, a dataset, a review — merged by maintainers outside its own cluster. Every merge carries the reviewer's stake, slashed if the work proves fake or copied. A Sybil farmer cannot mint cheap identities: each one must produce real, accepted work at full cost, and its standing withers if the grove stops vouching for it, and cloned accounts share one harvest.
